title: Sonata
identity: Daniel Schnyder’s Sonata for Soprano Saxophone and Piano is the soprano work in Edition Kunzelmann GM1725A, issued as a 36-page score and part. Carlos Felipe Vina’s 2015 University of Miami DMA guide concerns the composer’s subsequent bassoon adaptation; it reports the bassoon version’s multiphonics and Latin-jazz/Balkan influences, but those instrument-specific analysis details should not be transferred to the soprano score.

evidence.claim: Edition record identifies soprano saxophone and piano, Kunzelmann GM1725A, 36 pages.
Composer’s work list mentions the soprano saxophone sonata as recorded by Daniel Schnyder and Kenny Drew Jr.

The 2015 University of Miami DMA dissertation is a performance guide to Schnyder’s bassoon-and-piano version. Its abstract says the composer adapted the sonata from the original soprano saxophone version in collaboration with Martin Kuuskmann; technical discussion is about the bassoon version.
evidence.source_name: Carlos Felipe Vina, University of Miami DMA dissertation (bassoon version)

evidence.claim: Page preview visibly shows the soprano saxophone and piano score, first movement marked q=112, with a slurred saxophone line above a rhythmically active piano part. Product details identify Edition Kunzelmann GM-1725A and 36 pages.
evidence.source_name: Sheet Music Plus preview of Edition Kunzelmann

score_observations.observation: In the publisher/retailer preview’s first score page, the soprano part begins at quarter=112 with a slurred, moving melodic line over an active piano part with repeating rhythmic figures and chord changes. This is a limited opening-page sample, not a complete technical survey.

review_focus: Inference from the inspected opening page: assess coordination of the flowing, slurred soprano line against a rhythmically active piano part; a full score review is needed before judging later movements or the range.
collection_flag: The score preview inspected is the soprano saxophone and piano original, Edition Kunzelmann GM1725A. The University of Miami DMA guide concerns the subsequent bassoon adaptation; its bassoon-specific multiphonics and other technique findings are not evidence about the soprano saxophone edition.

listening.description: Composer lists a recording by Daniel Schnyder and Kenny Drew Jr.
listening.verification: Recording is cited in composer index; audio was not auditioned.

score_links.description: Edition Kunzelmann product page with visible page-1 score preview and edition details.

gaps: Only the first page of the soprano saxophone score was visually inspected; later movements, overall range, and complete technical demands remain unknown.
The University of Miami dissertation is a guide to the bassoon adaptation and cannot establish soprano-saxophone performance demands.
